question_text: A previously healthy 16-year-old boy comes to the physician because of a pruritic rash on the chest that has become progressively larger over the past 10 days. It is not painful. He is sexually active with two female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. He works part-time as a lifeguard. He has no family history of serious illness. He does not smoke. He drinks 5–6 beers on weekends. His temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 66/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. A photograph of the rash is shown below. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
